correctness.rationale: In round r the old burned vertices and their pairwise sums are contained in the span of the first r−1 sources, and the contemporaneous source can add only one vertex. For r≤m the resulting bound 2^(r−1) is insufficient. The same argument in round m+1 with a deficient prefix span excludes every dependent first-m tuple. Conversely, for an ordered basis, at the end of r≤m the burned set is exactly the nonzero preceding span plus the new basis vector: sums of the preceding basis vector with all old nonzero span vectors fill its coset, except for the vector itself which is already burned. The same final update fills the space before the last source can have any effect. There are 2^(m−1)−1 legal final choices for each ordered basis; the product and forced profile follow. Validity uses the previous round's burned set, not the set after current propagation. The recorded m=3,4 counts agree; no finite computation is used for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The labelled optimum-schedule count is a natural refinement of the established minimum-round invariant, with small instances already of computational interest. The result replaces finite enumeration with one structural description for arbitrary dimension and determines which rounds and choices matter. The basis product alone is routine; the contribution is identifying exactly the schedules to which it applies, including forced redundancy and its multiplicity.
residual_risks: Applies only to binary projective systems with synchronous round semantics and labelled sequences, not to automorphism classes or arbitrary designs.
